speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual given your leg position; acute appendicitis would not cause the leg to be shortened, flexed, and internally rotated. Did you experience any difficulty walking or bearing weight on the right leg immediately after the crash?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_hip
REQUEST IMAGES: Hip_Xray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_hip findings confirm a posterior dislocation of the right hip joint with associated soft tissue injury; Hip_Xray corroborates no fractures in the pelvic ring or femoral neck but confirms the posterior dislocation alignment.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior dislocation of the right hip joint. Based on the classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a rear-end collision, combined with MRI confirmation of dislocation without fracture, the primary injury is a posterior hip dislocation. While you mentioned knee pain, the hip findings are the critical diagnosis requiring immediate reduction and orthopedic consultation to prevent avascular necrosis.
